title: Startup founder pitch night
question: Is the self-serving bias pattern present? Answer yes or no.
input: At a pitch night, founder Lena says: 'Our app's viral growth last year happened because of the brilliant onboarding flow my team and I designed from scratch. We knew exactly what users needed. As for the slowdown this quarter, well, the entire ad market collapsed, Apple changed its tracking rules, and a competitor got bought by Google. Honestly, no one in our space could have grown through that. We're still the best team in the category.'

must_identify: viral growth attributed internally to team's design ability
slowdown attributed externally to ad market, Apple, competitor
same speaker is subject of both outcomes
both polarities (success and failure) are present
asymmetry serves self-image protection

title: Coach's halftime speech

title: Crate through the doorway

title: Shelf above the cabinet

title: Pipe through the wall

title: Train under the bridge

title: Painting and the doorway

input: A gallery assistant tried to carry a large rectangular painting through a standard interior doorway while keeping the painting upright (its long edge vertical). painting's long side is vertical when upright and must be ≤ 80 in or it wouldn't fit upright by height either

title: Books on the shelf

input: On a single shelf, four books stand upright in a row. The atlas is immediately to the left of the dictionary. The novel is immediately to the right of the dictionary. title: Greenhouse irrigation trigger
question: Did the misting system activate this morning? Answer yes or no.
input: The greenhouse manual states: if the soil moisture sensor reads below 20 percent, the misting system activates automatically. The sensor was calibrated last Tuesday by technician Hale, who noted that misting often correlates with hotter afternoons. This morning at 6 a.m., the sensor logged a reading of 14 percent. reading of 14 percent affirms the antecedent

title: Customs clearance rule
question: Must container CX-882 be diverted to bay 4? Answer yes or no.

title: Scholarship eligibility clause

title: Surgeon before difficult call

title: Negotiator at the table
question: Does the passage contain an instance of Ruiz regulating his own emotion? Answer yes or no.

title: Two siblings after bad news

title: Teacher and disruptive student

title: Author at hostile reading

both trigger and deliberate modulation are present

title: Father after child's tantrum
question: Which character's behavior is the clearest example of emotional self-regulation?
input: When his four-year-old hurled a bowl of pasta at the wall, Theo felt fury rise. He turned away, walked to the porch, and stood gripping the railing while he forced his jaw to unclench and counted backwards from twenty. Meanwhile, his partner crouched beside their daughter, speaking softly and rubbing her back to help her settle. After a few minutes, Theo came back inside and quietly began cleaning the floor with their daughter's help.

must_identify: Theo has a clear trigger (fury at the thrown bowl)
Theo's self-directed actions: walking away, unclenching jaw, counting backwards
the partner's soothing targets the daughter, not the partner's own emotion
self-regulation requires the modulation to be aimed at the self

title: Marble on tilted tray
question: While the tray remains tilted, in which direction does the marble move: toward the cat's edge or toward the opposite edge?
input: Renu sets a smooth wooden tray flat on her dining table and places a glass marble in the center. Her cat Pixel jumps onto one edge of the tray, pressing that edge down so the tray now slopes steadily from the cat's side toward the opposite side. The marble has no glue, no groove, and nothing blocking it. The tray surface is dry and polished. Renu watches without touching anything. The cat holds its position, keeping the tilt steady for several seconds before jumping off.

must_identify: the tray is tilted with the cat's side higher pressed down... actually cat presses edge down so cat's side is lower
gravity pulls the marble down the slope
the marble rolls toward the lower edge, which is the cat's edge

title: Ice cube in warm tea
question: Is the ice cube smaller than when he dropped it in? Answer yes or no.
input: Hassan pours hot black tea into a ceramic mug and, before drinking, drops a single ice cube into it. The mug sits on the kitchen counter for two minutes while he answers a phone call. The kitchen is a normal room temperature. No one stirs the mug, adds anything else, or moves it. When Hassan returns, he glances into the mug to check on the ice cube before taking a sip.

must_identify: hot tea transfers heat to the ice
ice melts when warmed
after two minutes the cube has shrunk

title: Cork released underwater
question: Once released, does the cork rise to the surface, stay in place, or sink further? Answer in one phrase.
input: At a swimming pool, Lila holds a dry wine cork at the bottom of the deep end, pressing it against the tiled floor with her fingertip. The pool water is still. Around her, swimmers above are doing slow laps, but no one is near her. Lila lifts her finger off the cork without pushing it in any direction. She keeps her hand still and watches the cork.

must_identify: cork is less dense than water
buoyancy exceeds gravity for cork
released cork floats upward to the surface

title: Bus brakes and standing rider
question: Relative to the bus, does Aiyana's upper body lurch forward or backward?
input: Aiyana is standing in the aisle of a city bus, not holding any pole, while the bus drives forward at a steady speed. Ahead, a delivery truck suddenly stops in the lane. The bus driver slams the brakes hard, and the bus decelerates sharply. Aiyana is not expecting the stop and her feet remain planted on the floor due to friction with her shoes, but nothing else restrains her body. Other seated passengers are belted in.

must_identify: bus decelerates suddenly
her body's inertia keeps it moving forward
relative to the bus, she pitches forward

title: Dropped ceramic plate
question: What should Theo most urgently warn his son about when he enters the kitchen? Answer in one short phrase.
input: While drying dishes, Theo loses his grip on a thin ceramic dinner plate. It slips from chest height and falls onto a hard tile floor below. The plate is not wrapped or padded. Theo does not catch it. The kitchen is otherwise quiet, with no rugs or mats on the tile. The plate lands flat with a sharp sound. Theo's young son, hearing the noise, runs in barefoot from the living room to see what happened.

must_identify: ceramic plate falling onto hard tile shatters
broken shards are dangerous to bare feet
the urgent hazard is the sharp pieces, not the noise or the plate's loss

title: Helium balloon released indoors
question: Where does the released helium balloon end up?
input: At a birthday party, Mira is handed a helium-filled balloon on a short ribbon. The room has a tall ceiling and is otherwise calm — no fans, no open windows, no air vents blowing nearby. Distracted by the cake, Mira lets go of the ribbon entirely. The balloon was not weighted at the bottom. Other balloons in the room are tied to chairs and remain in place. Mira does not reach to grab the ribbon back.

must_identify: helium is less dense than air
an unrestrained helium balloon rises
in a closed room it stops at the ceiling

title: Pouring water from kettle
question: When the water reaches the spout, does it flow into the cup or remain in the kettle?
input: Devon fills an electric kettle with cold water and sets it to boil. Once it clicks off, he lifts the kettle by its handle and tilts the spout over an empty teacup that sits on the counter directly below the spout's tip. He keeps the spout aimed at the cup and continues tilting until the water inside the kettle reaches the spout opening. The cup is wide-mouthed and clean. Devon does not move the cup.

must_identify: tilting brings water past the spout's lip
gravity pulls the water out and downward
water lands in the cup positioned below

title: Two balls down a ramp
question: Do the two balls reach the bottom at roughly the same time, or does one arrive much sooner? Answer in one short phrase.
input: On a wooden plank propped against a stack of books, Owen sets up a simple ramp. At the top, he holds two balls side by side: a solid rubber ball and a steel ball bearing of the same size. He releases both at exactly the same instant. The ramp is smooth and clean, the room is still, and neither ball is given any push. Both roll freely down the same slope to the floor. Owen films the run on his phone to settle a bet with his sister, who insists one ball will clearly beat the other to the bottom.

must_identify: common intuition correctly says heavier and lighter objects fall/roll together under gravity in everyday conditions
the trap is assuming the heavier steel ball wins by a wide margin
on a smooth ramp both balls arrive at nearly the same time

title: Book on a moving skateboard
question: Relative to the skateboard's original direction of motion, which way does the book slide off?
input: In an empty hallway, Priya places a hardcover book flat on top of a skateboard. She gives the skateboard a strong, steady push forward and lets go. The skateboard rolls smoothly across the level floor. The book is not glued, taped, or held — it just rests on the deck. Suddenly the front wheels of the skateboard hit a small raised threshold strip across the floor, and the skateboard stops abruptly. The book was not touching anything else.

must_identify: skateboard halts suddenly
the book's inertia keeps it moving forward
the book slides off the front of the deck

title: Hot pan on cold counter
question: Compared to when he set it down, is the skillet hotter, about the same, or cooler when he returns?
input: After frying eggs, Marco lifts a hot cast-iron skillet straight off the burner and sets it down on the granite countertop with no trivet or towel underneath. He immediately walks away to answer the door. The skillet was hot enough to make oil sputter just moments before. The granite countertop is at normal room temperature. The kitchen is otherwise undisturbed; no one touches the pan. Marco returns about fifteen minutes later and reaches for the skillet's handle to wash it.

must_identify: heat flows from hot skillet to cooler surroundings and counter
with the burner off, no new heat is added
after fifteen minutes the skillet has cooled noticeably
